A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AC3D. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, ablations, a user study, motion-spectrum analyses, and camera-pose linear-probing experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds backbone-specific comparisons and motion analyses using CogVideoX.

M1.justification: Figure 2 changes the depicted inter-block camera connection: v1 propagates features from before the DiT-XS block, whereas v3 propagates its output. The accompanying method description otherwise retains the same components and schedules. The PDFs do not establish whether this represents an implementation change or a schematic correction.

E1.justification: Both versions retain RealEstate10K, MSR-VTT, the 20K curated dynamic videos with stationary cameras, and the same generation and pose-analysis tasks. The CogVideoX additions concern model configurations rather than new datasets, domains, or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 2 substantially expands the comparison on the authors' VDiT backbone by adding MotionCtrl and CameraCtrl alongside VD3D. In v1, MotionCtrl and CameraCtrl were evaluated only with U-Net backbones. The original comparator configurations remain.

E3.justification: v3 adds CogVideoX-based evaluations and VDiT configurations for MotionCtrl and CameraCtrl, extending the backbone settings and shared-backbone controls. The existing benchmark metrics, reported training budgets, linear-probing split, and user-study design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C and Figures 7–8 repeat the motion-type spectrum and denoising-time analyses on CogVideoX, checking whether the findings extend beyond the original VDiT. The existing ablations, VDiT motion analyses, and linear probing are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 95% confidence intervals for Figure 3. No changed seed information, repeated-run counts, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported; the additional plots extend the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds four result rows: VD3D and AC3D on CogVideoX, plus MotionCtrl and CameraCtrl on VDiT. For example, the new CogVideoX comparison reports MSR-VTT FVD of 116.04 for AC3D versus 148.11 for VD3D. New motion-spectrum results also appear. All original Table 2 values and Table 1 preferences are unchanged.

T1.justification: The separate-guidance equation and camera-scale optimization remain mathematically unchanged. Replacing y with t for the text condition is a notation change. No new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three central contributions: motion-informed conditioning schedules, selective layer conditioning, and dynamic training-data supplementation. The headline quality, camera-control, and efficiency claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly interprets the similar CogVideoX motion patterns as evidence that the findings generalize beyond the original backbone. The existing explanations and limitations concerning out-of-distribution trajectories, optical-flow sensitivity, and linear probing remain.

D1.justification: Section 3.6 newly states that a tensor is zeroed for unconditional generation. Figure 3's expanded caption specifies temporal frequency and averaging across spatial, temporal-offset, and video-batch dimensions. Existing training, hardware, and data-construction details are retained; detailed settings for the added backbone experiments remain sparse.

R1.justification: v3 adds CAT3D and CAT4D citations. It also gives the already-cited DimensionX a specific discussion of transformer-based space/time control and predefined, noncontinuous camera trajectories. Most other reference changes are bibliographic updates or duplicate removal.

P1.justification: The main text receives copyediting and clearer explanations of VDiT-CC versus AC3D and noise truncation. The temporal encoder description moves to Appendix D.3, user-study instructions move to Appendix J, and acknowledgements are added. The main narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figure 2, expands Figure 3's caption, groups Table 2 by backbone with additional rows, and adds CogVideoX Figures 7–8. Existing appendix figures are retained as Figures 9–11. These are localized display changes within the same overall layout.

improvement.justification: The additional comparisons on a shared VDiT backbone and the CogVideoX performance and motion analyses strengthen comparison fairness and evidence of transfer beyond one model. Clarifications also improve readability. These are useful but limited gains: the original results and limitations remain, while sparse settings for the added experiments and the unexplained Figure 2 wiring change constrain reproducibility.
